nodes.name: Configuration space $S_N$ and normalized surface measure $\lambda_N$
nodes.statement: For given $N\geq 1,$ we denote by $S_N=\{\vsi\in\mathbb{R}^N:\|\vsi\|=\sqrt{N}\}$ the configuration space and by $\lambda_N$ its normalized surface measure.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: Pure $p$-spin Hamiltonian $H_{N,p}$
nodes.statement: Consider the pure $p$-spin Hamiltonians $H_{N,p}(\vsi)$ for $p\geq 1$ indexed by $\vsi\in S_N,$ \begin{align} H_{N,p}(\vsi)=\frac{1}{N^{(p-1)/2}}\sum_{1\leq i_1,\ldots,i_p\leq N}g_{i_1,\ldots,i_p}\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_p}, \end{align} where the random variables $g_{i_1,\ldots,i_p}$ for all $p\geq 1$ and all $(i_1,\ldots,i_p)$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian.
nodes.statement_short: The pure $p$-spin Hamiltonian is a normalized sum of i.i.d. Gaussian couplings against $p$-fold spin products.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: Hamiltonian of the mixed $p$-spin spherical model $H_N$
nodes.statement: The Hamiltonian of the mixed $p$-spin spherical model is given by \begin{align} H_N(\vsi)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p H_{N,p}(\vsi) \end{align}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: Decay condition on the mixture coefficients $(\beta_p)$
nodes.statement: with coefficients $(\beta_p)$ that satisfy $\beta_p\geq 0$ and decrease fast enough, $\sum_{p\geq 1}2^p\beta_p^2<\infty.$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: Overlap $R_{1,2}$ and covariance function $\xi$
nodes.statement: This technical assumption ensures that on $S_N$ the series $(\ref{eq2})$ converges a.s. and the covariance of the Gaussian process is given by a function of the normalized scalar product, called the overlap, $R_{1,2}=N^{-1}\sum_{i\leq N}\sigma_i^1\sigma_i^2$ of spin configurations $\vsi^1$ and $\vsi^2,$ $$ \mathbb{E}H_N(\vsi^1)H_N(\vsi^2)=N\xi(R_{1,2}), $$ where $\mathbb{E}$ is the expectation with respect to all Gaussian randomness and $\xi(x)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2 x^p.$
nodes.statement_short: The covariance of $H_N$ at two configurations is $N\xi(R_{1,2})$, where $R_{1,2}$ is the normalized scalar product (the overlap).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: Distribution function $\vx$ of the triplet $(k,\mathbf{m},\mathbf{q})$
nodes.statement: Given $k\geq 1$, let $\mathbf{m}=(m_\ell)_{0\leq \ell\leq k}$ and $\mathbf{q}=(q_\ell)_{0\leq \ell\leq k+1}$ be two sequences satisfying \begin{align*} &0=m_0\leq m_1\leq\ldots\leq m_{k-1}\leq m_k=1,\\ &0=q_0\leq q_1\leq \ldots \leq q_k\leq q_{k+1}=1. \end{align*} One may think of the triplet $(k,\mathbf{m},\mathbf{q})$ as a distribution function $\vx$ on $\left[0,1\right]$ with $\vx(q)=m_\ell$ if $q_\ell\leq q<q_{\ell+1}$ for $0\leq \ell\leq k$ and $\vx(1)=1.$
nodes.statement_short: A Parisi parameter is a pair of nondecreasing sequences $(\mathbf{m},\mathbf{q})$, encoded as a distribution function $\vx$ on $[0,1]$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: The functional $\mathcal{P}$
nodes.statement: We define for $1\leq \ell\leq k,$ $$d_\ell=\sum_{\ell\leq p\leq k}m_p(\xi'(q_{p+1})-\xi'(q_p)).$$ For a given parameter $b>d_1,$ we define $D_\ell=b-d_\ell$ for $1\leq \ell\leq k$ and $D_{k+1}=b.$ Let $\theta(x)=x\xi'(x)-\xi(x).$ The formulation of the Parisi formula involves a functional $\mathcal{P}$ of the distribution function $\vx$, \begin{align*} \mathcal{P}(\vx)=\inf_{b>d_1}\frac{1}{2}\left(b-1-\log b+\frac{\xi'(q_1)}{D_1}+\sum_{1\leq \ell\leq k}\frac{1}{m_\ell}\log \frac{D_{\ell+1}}{D_\ell}-\sum_{1\leq \ell\leq k}m_\ell(\theta(q_{\ell+1})-\theta(q_{\ell}))\right), \end{align*} which is the limit of the Parisi functional described below.
nodes.statement_short: The limiting Parisi functional $\mathcal{P}(\vx)$, an infimum over $b>d_1$ of an explicit expression in $\xi,\theta,\mathbf{m},\mathbf{q}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: The Parisi functional $\mathcal{P}_M$
nodes.statement: For every $M\geq 1,$ let $\vz_p=(z_{p,1},\ldots,z_{p,M})$ for $0\leq p\leq k$ be centered Gaussian random vectors with $\mathbb{E}z_{p,i}z_{p,i'}=\delta_{i,i'}(\xi'(q_{p+1})-\xi'(q_p))$ for any $i\neq i'$ and let $(\vz_p)_{0\leq p\leq k}$ be independent of each other. Starting from \begin{align*} X_{k+1}^M=\log\int_{S_M}\exp \veps\cdot \left(\vz _0+\cdots+\vz _k\right)d\lambda_M(\veps), \end{align*} we define decreasingly for $0\leq p\leq k,$ \begin{align*} X_p^M=\frac{1}{m_p}\log\mathbb{E}_p \exp m_p X_{p+1}^M, \end{align*} where $\mathbb{E}_p$ denotes the expectation in the random vectors $(\vz_i)_{i\geq p}.$ When $m_p=0,$ this means $X_p^M=\mathbb{E}_p X_{p+1}^M.$ Set the Parisi functional $$ \mathcal{P}_M(x)=X_0^M-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{1\leq p\leq k}m_p(\theta(q_{p+1})-\theta(q_p)). $$
nodes.statement_short: Finite-$M$ Parisi functional built from the decreasing recursion $X_p^M=m_p^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}_p\exp m_pX_{p+1}^M$ on the sphere $S_M$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: Convergence of the Parisi functionals $\mathcal{P}_M\to\mathcal{P}$
nodes.statement: A series of nontrivial applications of elementary large deviation principle implies $\mathcal{P}(\vx)=\lim_{M\rightarrow\infty}\mathcal{P}_M(\vx)$ (see Proposition 3.1 \cite{Tal061}).
nodes.statement_short: A large-deviation computation gives $\mathcal{P}(\vx)=\lim_M\mathcal{P}_M(\vx)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: Partition function $Z_N$
nodes.statement: Let us denote the partition function of the model by $$ Z_N=\int_{S_N}\exp H_N(\vsi)d\lambda_N(\vsi). $$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: The Parisi formula
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N=\inf_{\vx}\mathcal{P}(\vx), \end{align} where the infimum is taken over all possible choices of $\vx$.
nodes.statement_short: The limiting free energy of the general mixed $p$-spin spherical model equals $\inf_{\vx}\mathcal{P}(\vx)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results
assumptions: with coefficients $(\beta_p)$ that satisfy $\beta_p\geq 0$ and decrease fast enough, $\sum_{p\geq 1}2^p\beta_p^2<\infty.$
conclusions: where the infimum is taken over all possible choices of $\vx$.

nodes.name: Free energy, Crisanti-Sommers representation and external field
nodes.statement: The quantity in the limit on the left-hand side of $(\ref{thm1:eq1})$ is usually called the free energy of this model and the formula on the right-hand side of $(\ref{thm1:eq1})$ is the famous Parisi formula in the spherical form, which is also known to have the Crisanti-Sommers representation \cite{CS92} (see Theorem 4.1 in \cite{Tal061}). Of course, one may also consider the model in the present of external field and prove the equation $(\ref{thm1:eq1}),$ but for the clarity of our discussion, we will only consider the Hamiltonian of the form $(\ref{eq2}).$
nodes.statement_short: The right-hand side of the Parisi formula also admits the Crisanti-Sommers representation; an external field could be included but is omitted for clarity.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results

nodes.name: The Gaussian families $\vz(\vsi)$ and $y(\vsi)$
nodes.statement: For $M,N\geq 1$, let us denote by $(\vz(\vsi)=(z_1(\vsi),\ldots,z_M(\vsi)):\vsi\in S_N)$ and $(y(\vsi):\vsi\in S_N)$ two independent families of centered Gaussian random variables with covariances \begin{align} \begin{split} \mathbb{E}z_i(\vsi^1)z_{i'}(\vsi^2)&=\delta_{i,i'}\xi'(R_{1,2}) \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}y(\vsi^1)y(\vsi^2)&=\theta(R_{1,2}) \end{split} \end{align} for every $\vsi^1,\vsi^2\in S_N.$ These random variables are independent of all the other randomness.
nodes.statement_short: Two independent centered Gaussian families on $S_N$ with covariances $\delta_{i,i'}\xi'(R_{1,2})$ and $\theta(R_{1,2})$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Cavity Hamiltonian $H_{M,N}$ and Gibbs measure $G_{M,N}$
nodes.statement: Let $G_{M,N}$ be the Gibbs measure corresponding to the Hamiltonian \begin{align} H_{M,N}(\vsi)&=\sum_{p\geq 1}\frac{\beta_p}{(M+N)^{(p-1)/2}}\sum_{1\leq i_1,\ldots,i_p\leq N}g_{i_1,\ldots,i_{p}}\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_p} \end{align} with reference measure $\lambda_N$ on $S_N$ and let $\left<\cdot\right>_{M,N}$ be the Gibbs average of $G_{M,N}.$
nodes.statement_short: $H_{M,N}$ is the $N$-spin Hamiltonian normalized at scale $M+N$; $G_{M,N}$ is its Gibbs measure with reference measure $\lambda_N$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: The A.S.S. scheme
nodes.statement: For any $\delta>0$ and $M\geq 1,$ the lower limit of $N^{-1}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N$ is bounded from below by \begin{align} \begin{split} &\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\mathbb{E}\log \int_{S_M}\left<\exp \veps\cdot \vz (\vsi)\right>_{M,N}d\lambda_M(\veps)- \mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}y(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}\right)\\ &\qquad\qquad -\delta\xi'(1)+\frac{1}{M}\log \nu_M(A_\delta), \end{split} \end{align} where $\nu_M$ is the probability measure of the $M$-dimensional Gaussian density and $$ A_\delta=\{\veps\in\mathbb{R}^M:M\leq\|\veps\|^2\leq M(1+\delta)\}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Aizenman-Sims-Starr lower bound for the spherical model: the lower limit of the free energy dominates a cavity functional in $M$ coordinates minus $\delta\xi'(1)$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models
assumptions: where $\nu_M$ is the probability measure of the $M$-dimensional Gaussian density

nodes.name: Vanishing of $M^{-1}\log\nu_M(A_\delta)$ and the Ising analogue
nodes.statement: Note that a standard large deviation result yields $\lim_{M\rightarrow \infty}M^{-1}\log\nu_M(A_\delta)=0$ for every $\delta>0.$ Thus $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1})$ gives a lower bound for the lower limit of the free energy that will play an essential role in proving the Parisi formula in Section $\ref{proof}.$ Suppose that $\mu_N$ is the uniform probability measure on $\Sigma_N=\left\{-1,+1\right\}^N$. If we replace the measure space $(S_N,\lambda_N)$ by $(\Sigma_N,\mu_N)$ and ignore the error term $-\delta\xi'(1)+M^{-1}\log \nu_M(A_\delta)$ in $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1})$, then Theorem \ref{ASS:prop1} gives the A.S.S. scheme for the Ising spin glass model with general mixed $p$-spin interactions (see e.g. Section 15.8 \cite{Tal11}).
nodes.statement_short: The error term vanishes as $M\to\infty$, and replacing $(S_N,\lambda_N)$ by the hypercube recovers the classical Ising A.S.S. scheme.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Cavity decomposition of $H_{M+N}$ and the overlap $R(\vec{\omega},\vec{\omega}')$
nodes.statement: For $\vrho\in S_{M+N},$ let us write $\vrho=(\vsi,\veps)$ for the first $N$ coordinates $\vsi=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_N)$ and the last $M$ cavity coordinates $\veps=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_M)$ and write \begin{align*} H_{M+N}(\vrho)&=H_{M,N}(\vsi)+\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i Z_i(\vsi)+\gamma(\vrho), \end{align*} where $H_{M,N}$ is given in $(\ref{ASS:eq1}),$ the term $\varepsilon_iZ_i(\vsi)$ consists of all terms in $H_{M+N}$ with only one factor $\varepsilon_i$ from $\veps$ present, and the last term is the sum of terms with at least two factors in $\veps.$ From now on, without causing any ambiguity, for any given vectors $\vec{\omega},\vec{\omega}'\in\Bbb{R}^K$ for some $K\geq 1$, we define $R(\vec{\omega},\vec{\omega}')=K^{-1}\sum_{i\leq K}\omega_i\omega_i'.$
nodes.statement_short: Splitting $\vrho=(\vsi,\veps)$ into $N$ spin and $M$ cavity coordinates decomposes $H_{M+N}$ into $H_{M,N}$, a linear cavity term, and a remainder $\gamma$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Covariance identities for $H_{M,N}$, $Z_i$ and $\gamma$
nodes.statement: One can check easily that \begin{align} \begin{split} \mathbb{E}H_{M,N}(\vsi^1)H_{M,N}(\vsi^2)&=(M+N)\xi\left(\frac{N}{M+N}R(\vsi^1,\vsi^2)\right), \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}Z_i(\vsi^1)Z_i(\vsi^2)&=\xi'\left(\frac{N}{M+N}R(\vsi^1,\vsi^2)\right), \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}\gamma(\vrho)^2&\leq \frac{M^2}{M+N}\xi''(1). \end{split} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Covariances of the three cavity pieces, with $\mathbb{E}\gamma(\vrho)^2\leq M^2\xi''(1)/(M+N)$ negligible.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Cavity reduction of the lower limit of the free energy
nodes.statement: Let us notice an elementary fact that for a real-valued sequence $(c_N)$, if $\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}c_N/N=r\in\mathbb{R},$ then $M^{-1}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}(c_{M+N}-c_N)\leq r$ for every $M\geq 1.$ This implies \begin{align} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}\log Z_N}{N}\geq\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{Z_N} \end{align} and thus to obtain Theorem $\ref{ASS:prop1}$, it suffices to prove that $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1})$ is the lower bound of the right-hand side of $(\ref{ASS:main:eq0})$.
nodes.statement_short: Since $M^{-1}\liminf_N(c_{M+N}-c_N)\leq \liminf_N c_N/N$, it suffices to lower-bound $M^{-1}\liminf_N\mathbb{E}\log(Z_{M+N}/Z_N)$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Three-term decomposition of $\mathbb{E}\log Z_{M+N}/Z_N$
nodes.statement: Let us write $\mathbb{E}\log{Z_{M+N}}/{Z_N}$ as \begin{align} \begin{split} &\mathbb{E}\log \int_{A_\delta}\left< \exp\veps\cdot \vz(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}d\nu_M(\veps)-\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{S_N}\exp H_Nd\lambda_N(\vsi)}{\int_{S_N}\exp H_{M,N}d\lambda_N(\vsi)}\\ &+\mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}J_{M,N}d\nu_M(\veps)}, \end{split} \end{align} where \begin{align*} J_{M,N}(\veps)&=\int_{S_N}\exp(H_{M,N}(\vsi)+\veps\cdot \vz (\vsi))d\lambda_N(\vsi),\quad\veps\in\mathbb{R}^M. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb{E}\log(Z_{M+N}/Z_N)$ is written as a cavity term, a Hamiltonian-replacement term, and a measure-replacement term.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Lemma 1
nodes.statement: For $\vz\in\mathbb{R}^M,$ we have \begin{align} \int_{A_\delta}\exp \veps\cdot\vz d\nu_M(\veps)\geq \nu_M\left(A_\delta\right)\int_{S_M}\exp\veps\cdot \vz d\lambda_M(\veps). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Restricting the Gaussian measure to the shell $A_\delta$ dominates $\nu_M(A_\delta)$ times the spherical average of $\exp\veps\cdot\vz$.

nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Polar decomposition of $\nu_M$
nodes.statement: Using the rotational invariance of $\nu_M,$ there exists a probability measure $\gamma_M$ on $\mathbb{R}^+$ such that $\nu_M$ is the image of $\gamma_M\times \lambda_M$ under the map $(s,\veps) \mapsto s\veps.$
nodes.statement_short: Write $\nu_M$ as the image of a radial law times the uniform sphere measure.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Monotonicity in the radius
nodes.statement: For $1\leq s\leq (1+\delta)^{1/2}$, using symmetry, \begin{align*} \int \exp s\veps\cdot\vz d\lambda_M(\veps)&=\int \cosh(s\veps\cdot\vz)d\lambda_M(\veps)\\ &\geq \int \cosh(\veps\cdot\vz)d\lambda_M(\veps)=\int \exp \veps\cdot\vz d\lambda_M(\veps). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: By symmetry the spherical average equals a $\cosh$ average, which increases in $s\geq 1$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Integrate over the radial law
nodes.statement: Therefore, $(\ref{ASS:lem5:eq1})$ holds by \begin{align*} \int_{A_\delta}\exp \veps\cdot\vz d\nu_M(\veps)&=\int_{1}^{(1+\delta)^{1/2}}\int_{S_M}\exp s\veps\cdot \vz d\lambda_M(\veps)d\gamma_M(s)\\ &\geq\int_{1}^{(1+\delta)^{1/2}}\int_{S_M}\exp\veps\cdot \vz d\lambda_M(\veps)d\gamma_M(s)\\ &= \gamma_M(\{1\leq s\leq (1+\delta)^{1/2}\})\int_{S_M}\exp\veps\cdot \vz d\lambda_M(\veps). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrating the radial inequality over $\gamma_M$ yields the claimed bound.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Lower bound for the first term of the decomposition
nodes.statement: From this lemma and Fubini's theorem, the first term in $(\ref{ASS:main:eq1})$ is bounded from below by \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}\left<\exp \veps\cdot\vz(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}d\lambda_M(\veps)+\log \nu_M(A_\delta) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The cavity term dominates its spherical analogue plus $\log\nu_M(A_\delta)$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Lemma 2
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left|\mathbb{E}\log\frac{ \int_{S_N}\exp H_{N}(\vsi)d\lambda_N(\vsi)}{\int_{S_N}\exp H_{M,N}(\vsi)d\lambda_N(\vsi)} -\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp\sqrt{M}y(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}\right|=0. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Replacing $H_N$ by $H_{M,N}$ costs asymptotically exactly the Gibbs term $\mathbb{E}\log\langle\exp\sqrt{M}y(\vsi)\rangle_{M,N}$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Suppose $(y'(\vsi):\vsi\in S_N)$ is a family of centered Gaussian random variables independent of all the other randomness such that in distribution \begin{align*} H_N(\vsi)=H_{M,N}(\vsi)+\sqrt{M}y'(\vsi). \end{align*} It is easy to check that $\mathbb{E}y'(\vsi^1)y'(\vsi^2)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2D_pN^pR(\vsi^1,\vsi^2)^{p}$, where $$ D_{p}=\frac{1}{M}\left(\frac{1}{N^{p-1}}-\frac{1}{(M+N)^{p-1}}\right) $$ satisfies $N^pD_{p}\rightarrow p-1.$ Recall $y(\vsi)$ from $(\ref{ASS:eq0.2}).$ Let us consider the interpolating free energy \begin{align*} \psi(t)&=\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}\left(\sqrt{t}y'(\vsi)+\sqrt{1-t}{y}(\vsi)\right)\right>_{M,N}. \end{align*} Then $|\psi(1)-\psi(0)|$ gives the quantity in the limit on the left-hand side of $(\ref{ASS:lem4:eq1})$. Thus it suffices to prove that $\psi'(t)\rightarrow 0$ uniformly in $t\in (0,1)$ as $N\rightarrow\infty,$ which can be easily verified by using Gaussian integration by parts, as $N\rightarrow\infty,$ \begin{align*} \sup_{0<t<1}|\psi'(t)|&\leq M\sup_{\vsi^1,\vsi^2\in S_N}|\mathbb{E}y'(\vsi^1)y'(\vsi^2)-\mathbb{E}y(\vsi^1)y(\vsi^2)|\\ &=M\sup_{\vsi^1,\vsi^2\in S_N}\left|\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2(D_{p}N^p-(p-1))R(\vsi^1,\vsi^2)^p\right|\rightarrow 0. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian interpolation between $y'$ and $y$: bound $\psi'(t)$ by the covariance discrepancy, which vanishes.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Introduce the auxiliary field $y'$
nodes.statement: Suppose $(y'(\vsi):\vsi\in S_N)$ is a family of centered Gaussian random variables independent of all the other randomness such that in distribution \begin{align*} H_N(\vsi)=H_{M,N}(\vsi)+\sqrt{M}y'(\vsi). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $y'$ so that $H_N=H_{M,N}+\sqrt{M}y'$ in distribution.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Covariance of $y'$
nodes.statement: It is easy to check that $\mathbb{E}y'(\vsi^1)y'(\vsi^2)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2D_pN^pR(\vsi^1,\vsi^2)^{p}$, where $$ D_{p}=\frac{1}{M}\left(\frac{1}{N^{p-1}}-\frac{1}{(M+N)^{p-1}}\right) $$ satisfies $N^pD_{p}\rightarrow p-1.$
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\mathbb{E}y'y'$ and check $N^pD_p\to p-1$, so its covariance converges to $\theta$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Interpolating free energy $\psi(t)$
nodes.statement: Recall $y(\vsi)$ from $(\ref{ASS:eq0.2}).$ Let us consider the interpolating free energy \begin{align*} \psi(t)&=\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}\left(\sqrt{t}y'(\vsi)+\sqrt{1-t}{y}(\vsi)\right)\right>_{M,N}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define the interpolating free energy $\psi(t)$ between $y'$ and $y$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Uniform vanishing of $\psi'(t)$
nodes.statement: Then $|\psi(1)-\psi(0)|$ gives the quantity in the limit on the left-hand side of $(\ref{ASS:lem4:eq1})$. Thus it suffices to prove that $\psi'(t)\rightarrow 0$ uniformly in $t\in (0,1)$ as $N\rightarrow\infty,$ which can be easily verified by using Gaussian integration by parts, as $N\rightarrow\infty,$ \begin{align*} \sup_{0<t<1}|\psi'(t)|&\leq M\sup_{\vsi^1,\vsi^2\in S_N}|\mathbb{E}y'(\vsi^1)y'(\vsi^2)-\mathbb{E}y(\vsi^1)y(\vsi^2)|\\ &=M\sup_{\vsi^1,\vsi^2\in S_N}\left|\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2(D_{p}N^p-(p-1))R(\vsi^1,\vsi^2)^p\right|\rightarrow 0. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian integration by parts bounds $\sup_t|\psi'(t)|$ by the covariance gap, which tends to $0$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: The densities $F_{M,N}$, $F_M$ and the scaling factors $a_\ell$
nodes.statement: For $K\geq 1,$ we denote by $S_K^1$ the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^K$ and by $|S_K^1|$ the area of $S_K^1$. Set \begin{align*} A_{M,N}&=\prod_{j=1}^M\left[-\sqrt{M+N+1-j},\sqrt{M+N+1-j}\right],\\ b_{M,N}&=\prod_{j=1}^M\frac{|S_{M+N-j}^1|}{|S_{M+N+1-j}^1|\sqrt{M+N+1-j}}. \end{align*} Define \begin{align*} F_{M,N}(\veps)&=b_{M,N}\prod_{j=1}^M\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon_j^2}{M+N+1-j}\right)^{\frac{M+N-j-2}{2}},\quad\veps\in A_{M,N},\\ F_M(\veps)&=\left(\frac{1}{2\pi}\right)^{M/2}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\veps\|^2}{2}\right),\quad\veps\in \mathbb{R}^M. \end{align*} Define $a_1=1$ and for $2\leq \ell\leq M+1,$ $$ a_\ell(\veps)=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell-1}\sqrt{1+\frac{1-\varepsilon_j^2}{M+N-j}},\quad \veps\in A_{M,N}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Explicit product density $F_{M,N}$ on the cavity box $A_{M,N}$, its Gaussian limit $F_M$, and the radial correction factors $a_\ell(\veps)$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Suppose that $f$ is a nonnegative function defined on $S_{M+N}.$ Then we have \begin{align} \int_{S_{M+N}}f(\vrho)d\lambda_{M+N}(\vrho) &=\int_{A_{M,N}} F_{M,N}(\veps)d\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}\int_{S_N}f\left(\vsi a_{M+1},\varepsilon_{1}a_{1},\ldots,\varepsilon_Ma_M\right)d\lambda_{N}(\vsi). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Exact decoupling of $\lambda_{M+N}$ into the cavity density $F_{M,N}$ on $A_{M,N}$ times $\lambda_N$ on $S_N$, with rescaling $a_\ell$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models
assumptions: Suppose that $f$ is a nonnegative function defined on $S_{M+N}.$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: This is an elementary calculus formula that follows by an induction argument starting from \begin{align*} \int_{S_K}f(\vrho)d\lambda_K(\vrho)&=\frac{|S_{K-1}^1|}{|S_K^1|\sqrt{K}}\int_{-\sqrt{K}}^{\sqrt{K}}\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon^2}{K}\right)^{\frac{K-3}{2}}d\varepsilon \int_{S_{K-1}}f\left(\vsi \sqrt{\frac{K-\varepsilon^2}{K-1}},\varepsilon\right)d\lambda_{K-1}(\vsi) \end{align*} for every $K\geq 2.$
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the dimension from the one-coordinate slicing formula for $\lambda_K$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Weak convergence of the cavity coordinates
nodes.statement: As an immediate consequence of Lemma \ref{ASS:lem1}, the cavity coordinates converge weakly to the $M$-dimensional standard Gaussian random vector as $N$ tends to infinity.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models
assumptions: As an immediate consequence of Lemma \ref{ASS:lem1}
conclusions: the cavity coordinates converge weakly to the $M$-dimensional standard Gaussian random vector as $N$ tends to infinity.

nodes.name: Splitting of the third term
nodes.statement: We write $\mathbb{E}\log {Z_{M+N}}/{\int_{A_\delta}J_{M,N}d\nu_M(\veps)}$ as \begin{align} &\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\veps}+\mathbb{E}\log \frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\veps}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\veps}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The third term splits into a Hamiltonian-interpolation term and a density-replacement term $F_{M,N}$ versus $F_M$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Lemma 4
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\veps} \geq -M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The first term of the split is asymptotically at least $-M\delta\xi'(1)$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models
assumptions: where for $\vrho=(\vsi,\veps)$ with $\vsi\in S_N$ and $\veps\in A_\delta,$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Suppose that $(H_{M,N}'(\vsi):\vsi\in S_N)$ is an independent copy of $(H_{M,N}(\vsi):\vsi\in S_N)$ and is independent of all the other randomness. We consider the following interpolating Hamiltonian \begin{align*} \varphi(t)=&\mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}(\veps)d\veps\int_{S_N}\exp(H_{1,t}(\vrho)+H_{2,t}(\vrho)+H_{3,t}(\vrho))d \lambda_N(\vsi), \end{align*} where for $\vrho=(\vsi,\veps)$ with $\vsi\in S_N$ and $\veps\in A_\delta,$ \begin{align*} H_{1,t}(\vrho)&=\sqrt{t}H_{M,N}(\vsi a_{M+1})+\sqrt{1-t}H_{M,N}'(\vsi)\\ H_{2,t}(\vrho)&=\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i\left(\sqrt{t}a_i Z_i(\vsi a_{M+1})+\sqrt{1-t}z_i(\vsi)\right)\\ H_{3,t}(\vrho)&=\sqrt{t}\gamma(\vsi a_{M+1},\varepsilon_1a_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_Ma_M). \end{align*} From $(\ref{ASS:lem1:eq1})$, obviously $\varphi(1)\leq\mathbb{E}\log Z_{M+N}$ when $N$ is large enough. On the other hand, using Gaussian integration by parts and replicas $\vrho^1=(\vsi^1,\veps^1)$ and $\vrho^2=(\vsi^2,\veps^2),$ it follows that \begin{align*} \varphi'(t)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j\leq 3}\left(\mathbb{E}\left<U_{j}(\vrho,\vrho)\right>_t-\mathbb{E}\left<U_j(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)\right>_t\right), \end{align*} where $\left<\cdot\right>_t$ is the Gibbs average corresponding to random weights $F_{M,N}\exp(H_{1,t}+H_{2,t}+H_{3,t})$ with reference measure $\lambda_N\times d\veps$ on $S_N\times A_\delta$ and \begin{align*} U_1(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)&=\mathbb{E}H_{M,N}(\vsi^1a_{M+1}(\veps^1))H_{M,N}(\vsi^2a_{M+1}(\veps^2))- \mathbb{E}H_{M,N}'(\vsi^1)H_{M,N}'(\vsi^2)\\ U_2(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)&=\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i^1\varepsilon_i^2\left(a_i(\veps^1)a_{i}(\veps^2)\mathbb{E}Z_i(\vsi^1a_{M+1}(\veps^1))Z_i(\vsi^2a_{M+1}(\veps^2)) -\mathbb{E}z_i(\vsi^1)z_i(\vsi^2)\right)\\ U_3(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)&=\mathbb{E}\gamma(\vsi^1a_{M+1}(\veps^1),\eps_1^1a_1(\veps^1),\ldots,\eps_M^1a_M(\veps^1))\\ &\qquad\cdot\gamma(\vsi^2a_{M+1}(\veps^2),\eps_1^2a_1(\veps^2),\ldots,\eps_M^2a_M(\veps^2)). \end{align*} From $(\ref{ASS:eq0.1})$, $(\ref{ASS:eq2.2}),$ and $(\ref{ASS:eq2.3})$, it is easy to see that for $j=2,3,$ $$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{\vrho^1,\vrho^2\in S_N\times A_\delta}|U_j(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)|\rightarrow 0$$ and from $(\ref{ASS:eq2.1})$ and using mean value theorem, \begin{align*} &\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{\vrho^1,\vrho^2\in S_N\times A_\delta}|U_1(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)|\\ &\leq \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\xi'(1)(M+N)\sup_{\veps^1,\veps^2\in A_\delta}\left|\frac{N}{M+N}a_{M+1}(\veps^1)a_{M+1}(\veps^2)-1\right|\\ &=\xi'(1)\sup_{\veps^1,\veps^2\in A_\delta}\left|M-\frac{\|\veps^1\|^2+\|\veps^2\|^2}{2}\right|\leq M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align*} Thus we conclude that $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{0<t<1}|\varphi'(t)|\leq M\delta\xi'(1)$ and so $(\ref{ASS:lem2:eq1})$ follows by \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\veps}&\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}(\varphi(1)-\varphi(0))\\ &\geq -\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{0<t<1}|\varphi'(t)|\geq -M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian interpolation $\varphi(t)$ between the rescaled and the decoupled Hamiltonians; the covariance discrepancy is at most $M\delta\xi'(1)$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Construct the interpolating Hamiltonian $\varphi(t)$
nodes.statement: Suppose that $(H_{M,N}'(\vsi):\vsi\in S_N)$ is an independent copy of $(H_{M,N}(\vsi):\vsi\in S_N)$ and is independent of all the other randomness. We consider the following interpolating Hamiltonian \begin{align*} \varphi(t)=&\mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}(\veps)d\veps\int_{S_N}\exp(H_{1,t}(\vrho)+H_{2,t}(\vrho)+H_{3,t}(\vrho))d \lambda_N(\vsi), \end{align*} where for $\vrho=(\vsi,\veps)$ with $\vsi\in S_N$ and $\veps\in A_\delta,$ \begin{align*} H_{1,t}(\vrho)&=\sqrt{t}H_{M,N}(\vsi a_{M+1})+\sqrt{1-t}H_{M,N}'(\vsi)\\ H_{2,t}(\vrho)&=\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i\left(\sqrt{t}a_i Z_i(\vsi a_{M+1})+\sqrt{1-t}z_i(\vsi)\right)\\ H_{3,t}(\vrho)&=\sqrt{t}\gamma(\vsi a_{M+1},\varepsilon_1a_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_Ma_M). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Interpolate between the rescaled cavity Hamiltonian and an independent decoupled copy.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Endpoint $t=1$ dominated by $\mathbb{E}\log Z_{M+N}$
nodes.statement: From $(\ref{ASS:lem1:eq1})$, obviously $\varphi(1)\leq\mathbb{E}\log Z_{M+N}$ when $N$ is large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3 identifies $\varphi(1)$ with a lower bound for $\mathbb{E}\log Z_{M+N}$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Derivative formula via Gaussian integration by parts
nodes.statement: On the other hand, using Gaussian integration by parts and replicas $\vrho^1=(\vsi^1,\veps^1)$ and $\vrho^2=(\vsi^2,\veps^2),$ it follows that \begin{align*} \varphi'(t)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j\leq 3}\left(\mathbb{E}\left<U_{j}(\vrho,\vrho)\right>_t-\mathbb{E}\left<U_j(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)\right>_t\right), \end{align*} where $\left<\cdot\right>_t$ is the Gibbs average corresponding to random weights $F_{M,N}\exp(H_{1,t}+H_{2,t}+H_{3,t})$ with reference measure $\lambda_N\times d\veps$ on $S_N\times A_\delta$ and \begin{align*} U_1(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)&=\mathbb{E}H_{M,N}(\vsi^1a_{M+1}(\veps^1))H_{M,N}(\vsi^2a_{M+1}(\veps^2))- \mathbb{E}H_{M,N}'(\vsi^1)H_{M,N}'(\vsi^2)\\ U_2(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)&=\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i^1\varepsilon_i^2\left(a_i(\veps^1)a_{i}(\veps^2)\mathbb{E}Z_i(\vsi^1a_{M+1}(\veps^1))Z_i(\vsi^2a_{M+1}(\veps^2)) -\mathbb{E}z_i(\vsi^1)z_i(\vsi^2)\right)\\ U_3(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)&=\mathbb{E}\gamma(\vsi^1a_{M+1}(\veps^1),\eps_1^1a_1(\veps^1),\ldots,\eps_M^1a_M(\veps^1))\\ &\qquad\cdot\gamma(\vsi^2a_{M+1}(\veps^2),\eps_1^2a_1(\veps^2),\ldots,\eps_M^2a_M(\veps^2)). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate $\varphi$ to get replica covariance differences $U_1,U_2,U_3$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Estimates on $U_1$, $U_2$, $U_3$
nodes.statement: From $(\ref{ASS:eq0.1})$, $(\ref{ASS:eq2.2}),$ and $(\ref{ASS:eq2.3})$, it is easy to see that for $j=2,3,$ $$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{\vrho^1,\vrho^2\in S_N\times A_\delta}|U_j(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)|\rightarrow 0$$ and from $(\ref{ASS:eq2.1})$ and using mean value theorem, \begin{align*} &\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{\vrho^1,\vrho^2\in S_N\times A_\delta}|U_1(\vrho^1,\vrho^2)|\\ &\leq \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\xi'(1)(M+N)\sup_{\veps^1,\veps^2\in A_\delta}\left|\frac{N}{M+N}a_{M+1}(\veps^1)a_{M+1}(\veps^2)-1\right|\\ &=\xi'(1)\sup_{\veps^1,\veps^2\in A_\delta}\left|M-\frac{\|\veps^1\|^2+\|\veps^2\|^2}{2}\right|\leq M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $U_2,U_3$ vanish and the mean value theorem bounds $U_1$ by $M\delta\xi'(1)$ on the shell $A_\delta$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Conclude by the mean value bound
nodes.statement: Thus we conclude that $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{0<t<1}|\varphi'(t)|\leq M\delta\xi'(1)$ and so $(\ref{ASS:lem2:eq1})$ follows by \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\veps}&\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}(\varphi(1)-\varphi(0))\\ &\geq -\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{0<t<1}|\varphi'(t)|\geq -M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine $\varphi(1)-\varphi(0)$ with the uniform derivative bound.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Lemma 5
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\veps}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M}J_{M,N}d\veps}\geq 0. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Replacing the exact cavity density $F_{M,N}$ by the Gaussian density $F_M$ costs nothing asymptotically.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Using the inequality $\log(1-x)\geq -2x$ for $0<x<1/2,$ when $N$ is sufficiently large, we have for every $\veps\in A_\delta,$ \begin{align*} &\log \frac{F_{M,N}(\veps)}{F_M(\veps)}\\ &=\log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log\frac{1}{2\pi}+\sum_{j=1}^M\frac{M+N-j-2}{2}\log\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon_j^2}{M+N+1-j}\right)+\frac{\|\veps\|^2}{2}\\ &\geq \log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log\frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{3\|\veps\|^2}{M+N}. \end{align*} Note that $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}b_{M,N}=1/(2\pi)^{M/2}$ as can be seen from $(\ref{ASS:lem1:eq1})$ with $f=1.$ By Jensen's inequality, we obtain \begin{align*} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}\exp \left(\log F_{M,N}/F_{M}\right)d\veps}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\veps}\\ &\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}\log F_{M,N}/F_{M}d\veps}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\veps}\\ &\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log \frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{3M}{M+N}\right)=0 \end{align*} and this gives $(\ref{ASS:lem3:eq1}).$
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound $\log(F_{M,N}/F_M)$ elementarily, then apply Jensen's inequality and $b_{M,N}\to(2\pi)^{-M/2}$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Pointwise bound on $\log(F_{M,N}/F_M)$
nodes.statement: Using the inequality $\log(1-x)\geq -2x$ for $0<x<1/2,$ when $N$ is sufficiently large, we have for every $\veps\in A_\delta,$ \begin{align*} &\log \frac{F_{M,N}(\veps)}{F_M(\veps)}\\ &=\log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log\frac{1}{2\pi}+\sum_{j=1}^M\frac{M+N-j-2}{2}\log\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon_j^2}{M+N+1-j}\right)+\frac{\|\veps\|^2}{2}\\ &\geq \log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log\frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{3\|\veps\|^2}{M+N}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the log-ratio and bound it below using $\log(1-x)\geq-2x$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Normalizing constant converges
nodes.statement: Note that $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}b_{M,N}=1/(2\pi)^{M/2}$ as can be seen from $(\ref{ASS:lem1:eq1})$ with $f=1.$
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3 with $f=1$ to get $b_{M,N}\to(2\pi)^{-M/2}$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Jensen's inequality
nodes.statement: By Jensen's inequality, we obtain \begin{align*} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}\exp \left(\log F_{M,N}/F_{M}\right)d\veps}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\veps}\\ &\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}\log F_{M,N}/F_{M}d\veps}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\veps}\\ &\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log \frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{3M}{M+N}\right)=0 \end{align*} and this gives $(\ref{ASS:lem3:eq1}).$
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality moves the log inside and the resulting limit is $0$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: From $(\ref{ASS:main:eq0})$, $(\ref{ASS:main:eq1})$, and $(\ref{sec2:eq1}),$ using Lemmas $\ref{ASS:lem4},$ $\ref{ASS:lem2}$, and $\ref{ASS:lem3},$ the lower limit of $N^{-1}{\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N}}$ is bounded from below by \begin{align*} \frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}\left<\exp \veps\cdot\vz(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}d\nu_M(\veps)-\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp\sqrt{M}y(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}\right)-\delta\xi'(1) \end{align*} and then $(\ref{ASS:lem5.1:eq1})$ yields $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1}).$
nodes.statement_short: Assemble the three-term decomposition with Lemmas 2, 4 and 5, then apply Lemma 1's spherical bound.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Combine the lemmas into a Gaussian-shell bound
nodes.statement: From $(\ref{ASS:main:eq0})$, $(\ref{ASS:main:eq1})$, and $(\ref{sec2:eq1}),$ using Lemmas $\ref{ASS:lem4},$ $\ref{ASS:lem2}$, and $\ref{ASS:lem3},$ the lower limit of $N^{-1}{\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N}}$ is bounded from below by \begin{align*} \frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}\left<\exp \veps\cdot\vz(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}d\nu_M(\veps)-\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp\sqrt{M}y(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}\right)-\delta\xi'(1) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 2, 4, 5 give the bound with the Gaussian measure $\nu_M$ on $A_\delta$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models

nodes.name: Pass to the spherical measure
nodes.statement: and then $(\ref{ASS:lem5.1:eq1})$ yields $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1}).$
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 1 converts to the spherical integral.

nodes.name: Guerra's replica symmetry breaking upper bound
nodes.statement: Our argument is started with Guerra's replica symmetry breaking interpolation scheme in the spherical models (see Section 3 in \cite{Tal061}). In the case when $p$-spin interactions for odd $p\geq 3$ are not present in $(\ref{eq2})$, this scheme implies that the upper limit of the free energy is bounded from above by $\inf_{\vx}\mathcal{P}(\vx).$ The fact that this bound still holds in the general mixed $p$-spin case relies on Talagrand's positivity principle on the overlap (see \cite{Tal03} and Section 12.3 in \cite{Tal11}) that is deduced from the validity of the G.G. identities \cite{GG98} derived by a perturbation trick on the Hamiltonian.
nodes.statement_short: Guerra's interpolation plus Talagrand's positivity principle give the matching upper bound $\limsup_N N^{-1}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N\leq\inf_{\vx}\mathcal{P}(\vx)$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
assumptions: In the case when $p$-spin interactions for odd $p\geq 3$ are not present in $(\ref{eq2})$
conclusions: this scheme implies that the upper limit of the free energy is bounded from above by $\inf_{\vx}\mathcal{P}(\vx).$

nodes.name: The upper bound argument is well-known
nodes.statement: This part of the argument is well-known and has been used in several places. For example, the readers are referred to Theorem 14.4.4 \cite{Tal11} for a great detailed discussion.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Why all $M\geq 1$ are needed in the spherical model
nodes.statement: Our main concern in the proof will be concentrated on obtaining the lower bound, that is, the lower limit of the free energy is bounded from below by $\inf_{\vx}\mathcal{P}(\vx)$, that will be established in several steps and is based on the A.S.S. scheme. Again due to the non-product structure of the uniform measure on the sphere, additional technical issues occur. For instance, in the Ising spin glass model, the argument for the lower bound only uses the A.S.S. scheme with a single cavity coordinate, that is $M=1$ (see Theorem 3.5 \cite{AC10}, Lemma 11 \cite{Pan10:2}, or Proposition 2 \cite{Pan11:1}), but this is not the case in our model. Indeed, recalling the formulation of the Parisi formula in the spherical model, one may figure out immediately that it is necessary to deal with the A.S.S. scheme $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1})$ with all $M\geq 1$ and compute their lower limit in $M.$ Under this circumstance, we find the fact that the Parisi functionals $(\mathcal{P}_M)_{M\geq 1}$ have the same Lipschitz constant with respect to the $L_1$-norm as stated in Lemma $\ref{AGM:prop21}$ below is of great use.
nodes.statement_short: Unlike the Ising case where $M=1$ suffices, the spherical model requires the A.S.S. scheme for all $M$ and a uniform Lipschitz property of $\mathcal{P}_M$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Perturbation Hamiltonians $H_N^{pert}$, $H_{M,N}^{pert}$ and the measure $G_{M,N}^-$
nodes.statement: For each $u=(u_p)_{p\geq 1}$ with $1\leq u_p\leq 2,$ let us consider a perturbation Hamiltonian \begin{align*} H_{N}^{pert}(\vsi)=\frac{1}{N^{1/8}}\sum_{p\geq 1}\frac{u_p}{2^p}H_{N,p}'(\vsi), \end{align*} where $H_{N,p}'(\vsi)$ are independent copies of the $p$-spin Hamiltonian in $(\ref{eq1})$. Since the perturbation term is of a small order, replacing $H_N$ with $H_N+H_N^{pert}$ in $(\ref{thm1:eq1})$ obviously does not affect the limit and in addition, the following A.S.S. scheme also holds. Consider another perturbation Hamiltonian \begin{align*} H_{M,N}^{pert}(\vsi)=\frac{1}{(M+N)^{1/8}}\sum_{p\geq 1}\frac{u_p}{2^p}\left(\frac{N}{M+N}\right)^{(p-1)/2}H_{N,p}'(\vsi). \end{align*} Let $G_{M,N}^-$ be the Gibbs measure corresponding to the Hamiltonian $H_{M,N}+H_{M,N}^{pert}$ with reference measure $\lambda_N$ and $\left<\cdot\right>_{M,N}^-$ be the average with respect to the product Gibbs measure $G_{M,N}^{-\otimes\infty}.$
nodes.statement_short: A small $N^{-1/8}$-order perturbation of the Hamiltonian, together with its perturbed Gibbs measure $G_{M,N}^-$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: The A.S.S. scheme for the perturbed Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: Recall $A_\delta$ and $\nu_M$ from Theorem $\ref{ASS:prop1}.$ For every $\delta>0$ and $M\geq 1,$ we have \begin{align} \begin{split} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N\\ &\geq\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{u}\left(\mathbb{E}\log \int_{S_M}\left<\exp \veps\cdot \vz (\vsi)\right>_{M,N}^-d\lambda_M(\veps)- \mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}y(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}^-\right)\\ &\qquad\qquad -\delta\xi'(1)+\frac{1}{M}\log \nu_M(A_\delta), \end{split} \end{align} where the supremum is taken over all $u=(u_{p})_{p\geq 1}$ with $1\leq u_p\leq 2.$
nodes.statement_short: The A.S.S. lower bound persists for the perturbed Gibbs measure, with a supremum over the perturbation parameters $u$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
assumptions: where the supremum is taken over all $u=(u_{p})_{p\geq 1}$ with $1\leq u_p\leq 2.$

nodes.name: Proof of the A.S.S. scheme for the perturbed Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: Starting with the Hamiltonian $H_{M+N}+H_{M+N}^{pert}$ and using the fact that $H_{M+N}^{pert}$ is of a small order, one may easily find that the same arguments in the proof of Theorem $\ref{ASS:prop1}$ also work in Proposition $\ref{ASS:cor}$, so we will leave this part of the proof to the readers.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the proof of Theorem 2 with the perturbed Hamiltonian, which is of lower order; details left to the reader.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: The G.G. discrepancy functional $\Phi_{M,N}(p,n,f)$
nodes.statement: In what follows, for each $M\geq 1$, we will construct a sequence $(u^{M,N})_{N\geq 1}$ for $u^{M,N}=(u_p^{M,N})_{p\geq 1}$ with $1\leq u_p^{M,N}\leq 2$ along which the G.G. identities for the Gibbs measure $G_{M,N}^-$ and the A.S.S. scheme for the Hamiltonian $H_{M,N}+H_{M,N}^{pert}$ hold simultaneously. Let $(\vsi^\ell)_{\ell\geq 1}$ be an i.i.d. sample from $G_{M,N}^-$ and let $R^{M,N}=(R_{\ell,\ell'}^{M,N})_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}$ be the normalized Gram matrix, or matrix of overlaps, of this sample. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the collection of all $(p,n,f)$ with $p\geq 1,$ $n\geq 2,$ and $f$ being a monomial of $(R_{\ell,\ell'}^{M,N})_{\ell,\ell'\leq n}.$ We define \begin{align*} &\Phi_{M,N}(p,n,f)\\ &=\left|\mathbb{E}\left<f(R_{1,n+1}^{M,N})^p\right>_{M,N}^--\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left<f\right>_{M,N}^- \mathbb{E}\left<(R_{1,2}^{M,N})^p\right>_{M,N}^--\frac{1}{n}\sum_{\ell=2}^n \mathbb{E}\left<f(R_{1,\ell}^{M,N})^p\right>_{M,N}^-\right| \end{align*} for $(p,n,f)\in \mathcal{C}.$
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_{M,N}(p,n,f)$ measures the failure of the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities for the overlap array of $G_{M,N}^-$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities
nodes.statement: For $M\geq 1$, we have \begin{align} \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N}(p,n,f)=0 \end{align} for all $(p,n,f)\in\mathcal{C},$ where we view $u=(u_p)_{p\geq 1}$ as a sequence of i.i.d. uniform random variables on $\left[1,2\right]$ and $\mathbb{E}_u$ is the expectation with respect to the randomness of $u.$
nodes.statement_short: Averaged over random perturbation parameters $u$, the G.G. discrepancy vanishes as $N\to\infty$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
assumptions: where we view $u=(u_p)_{p\geq 1}$ as a sequence of i.i.d. uniform random variables on $\left[1,2\right]$

nodes.name: The functionals $\Phi_{M,N}(u)$ and $\Lambda_{M,N}(u)$
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{C}$ is a countable set, we can enumerate it as $\left\{(p_j,n_j,f_j)\right\}_{j\geq 1}.$ Let us define \begin{align*} \Phi_{M,N}(u)&=\sum_{j\geq 1}\frac{1}{2^j}\Phi_{M,N}(p_j,n_j,f_j),\\ \Lambda_{M,N}(u)&=\frac{1}{M}\left(\mathbb{E}\log\int_{S_M}\left<\exp \veps\cdot\vz(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}^-d\lambda_M(\veps) -\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}y(\vsi)\right>_{M,N}^-\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A single weighted G.G. discrepancy $\Phi_{M,N}(u)$ and the cavity functional $\Lambda_{M,N}(u)$ appearing in the A.S.S. bound.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Simultaneous validity of the G.G. identities and the A.S.S. scheme along $(u^{M,N})$
nodes.statement: By Chebyshev's inequality, $\mathbb{P}_u(\Phi_{M,N}\leq \eta)\geq 1-\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N}/\eta$ for every $\eta>0.$ If we pick $\eta=2\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N},$ it implies that for any $M$ and $N$ we can always find $u^{M,N}=(u_p^{M,N})_{p\geq 1}$ such that $\Phi_{M,N}(u^{M,N})\leq 2\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N}$. Note that using $\Phi_{M,N}(n,p,f)\leq 2$ and the G.G. identities $(\ref{prop:GG:eq1})$ implies $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N}=0.$ Consequently, we have \begin{align} \begin{split} \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\Phi_{M,N}(u^{M,N})&=0 \end{split} \end{align} and from $(\ref{ASS:cor:eq1})$, $\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}N^{-1}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N$ is bounded from below by \begin{align} \begin{split} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\Lambda_{M,N}(u^{M,N})-\delta\xi'(1)+\frac{1}{M}\log \nu_M(A_\delta). \end{split} \end{align} In other words, for each $M\geq 1,$ both the G.G. identities and the A.S.S. scheme hold along $(u^{M,N})_{N\geq 1}$. Let us redefine the Hamiltonian $H_{M,N}^{pert}$ and the Gibbs measure $G_{M,N}^-$ by fixing parameters $u=u^{M,N}.$
nodes.statement_short: A Chebyshev argument selects parameters $u^{M,N}$ along which the G.G. identities hold and the A.S.S. lower bound is retained.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
conclusions: both the G.G. identities and the A.S.S. scheme hold along $(u^{M,N})_{N\geq 1}$.

nodes.name: Gram-de Finetti array and the limiting overlap array $R^M$
nodes.statement: Next, we will find a sequence of asymptotic Gibbs' measures that satisfy the G.G. identities and represent the lower limit in $(\ref{AGM:eq2.1})$. For each $M\geq 1,$ let us pick a subsequence $(N_n)$ along which the limits in $(\ref{AGM:eq2})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq2.1})$ are achieved and the distribution $R^{M,N}$ under $\mathbb{E}G_{M,N}^{-\otimes\infty}$ converges in the sense of convergence of finite dimensional distributions to the distribution of some array $R^M$. To lighten the notation, we assume without loss of generality that the sequence $(N_n)$ coincides with the natural numbers. Under $\mathbb{E}G_{M,N}^{-\otimes\infty}$, the array ${R}^{M,N}$ is weakly exchangeable, that is, \begin{align*} \left(R_{\pi(\ell),\pi(\ell')}^{M,N}\right)\stackrel{d}{=}\left(R_{\ell,\ell'}^{M,N}\right) \end{align*} for any permutation $\pi$ of finitely many indices. This property will still be preserved in the limit such that $R^M$ is a weakly exchangable symmetric non-negative definite array. Such an array is called a Gram-de Finetti array and is known to have the Dovbysh-Sudakov representation \cite{DS82}.
nodes.statement_short: Along a subsequence the overlap arrays converge to a weakly exchangeable, symmetric, non-negative definite array $R^M$ — a Gram-de Finetti array.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
nodes.genus: weakly exchangable symmetric non-negative definite array

nodes.name: The Dovbysh-Sudakov representation
nodes.statement: If $(R_{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}$ is a Gram-de Finetti array such that $R_{\ell,\ell}=1$, then there exists a random measure $G$ on the unit ball of a separable Hilbert space such that \begin{align*} \left(R_{\ell,\ell'}\right)_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}\stackrel{d}{=}\left(\vtau^{\ell}\cdot\vtau^{\ell'}+\delta_{\ell,\ell'}(1-\|\vtau^{\ell}\|^2)\right)_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}, \end{align*} where $(\vtau^\ell)$ is an i.i.d. sample from $G.$
nodes.statement_short: A Gram-de Finetti array with unit diagonal is generated by an i.i.d. sample from a random measure on the unit ball of a separable Hilbert space.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
assumptions: If $(R_{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}$ is a Gram-de Finetti array such that $R_{\ell,\ell}=1$
conclusions: then there exists a random measure $G$ on the unit ball of a separable Hilbert space such that \begin{align*} \left(R_{\ell,\ell'}\right)_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}\stackrel{d}{=}\left(\vtau^{\ell}\cdot\vtau^{\ell'}+\delta_{\ell,\ell'}(1-\|\vtau^{\ell}\|^2)\right)_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}, \end{align*} where $(\vtau^\ell)$ is an i.i.d. sample from $G.$

nodes.name: The asymptotic Gibbs measure $G_M$ and its G.G. identities
nodes.statement: Obviously the array $R^M$ satisfies $R_{\ell,\ell}^M=1.$ Using Proposition $\ref{AGM:Prop1}$, let us denote by $G_M$ the random measure generating the array $R^{M}$ and by $(\vtau^\ell)$ an i.i.d. sample from $G_M$. We also denote by $\left<\cdot\right>_M$ the average with respect to $G_M.$ From $(\ref{AGM:eq2})$ and an approximation argument, the measure $G_M$ satisfies the G.G. identities, \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\left<f\psi(R_{1,n+1}^M)\right>_M=\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left<f\right>_M\mathbb{E}\left<\psi(R_{1,2}^M)\right>_M+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{\ell=2}^n \mathbb{E}\left<f\psi(R_{1,\ell}^M)\right>_M \end{align} for all $n\geq 2,$ all bounded measurable function $f$ of $(R_{\ell,\ell'}^M)_{\ell,\ell'\leq n}$, and measurable function $\psi.$ These identities will be used to identify the asymptotic Gibbs measures $G_M$ in next subsection.
nodes.statement_short: $G_M$ is the random measure generating $R^M$; it inherits the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities in the limit.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: The functional $\Psi_M(\mathcal{L})$
nodes.statement: Let us continue to check that the limit of $\Lambda_{M,N}(u^{M,N})$ in $N$ can be expressed in terms of $G_{M},$ which relies on the following observation. Suppose for the moment that $R=(R_{\ell,\ell'})_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}$ is an arbitrary Gram-de Finetti array such that $R_{\ell,\ell}=1.$ Let $\mathcal{L}$ be its distribution and $G$ be any random measure generating $R$ as Proposition $\ref{AGM:Prop1}.$ Suppose that $\vz(\vtau)=(z_i(\vtau))_{i\leq M}$ and $y(\vtau)$ are two Gaussian processes on the unit ball of some Hilbert space generating $R$ with covariances \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}z_i(\vtau^1)z_{i'}(\vtau^2)=\delta_{i,i'}\xi'(\vtau^1\cdot\vtau^2),\,\,\mathbb{E}y(\vtau^1)y(\vtau^2)=\theta(\vtau^1\cdot\vtau^2), \end{align*} let $\veta$ be a $M$-dimensional standard Gaussian random vector, and let $\eta$ be a standard Gaussian random variable. Denote by $\left<\cdot\right>$ the Gibbs average corresponding to $G$ and define \begin{align*} \Psi_M(\mathcal{L})=&\frac{1}{M}\mathbb{E}\log \int_{S_M}\mathbb{E}_{\veta}\left<\exp\veps\cdot(\vz (\vtau)+\veta(\xi'(1)-\xi'(\|\vtau\|^2))^{1/2})\right>d\lambda_M(\veps)\\ &-\frac{1}{M}\mathbb{E}\log \mathbb{E}_\eta\left<\exp\sqrt{M}({y}(\vtau)+\eta(\xi'(1)-\xi'(\|\vtau\|^2))^{1/2})\right>. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $\Psi_M(\mathcal{L})$ is the cavity functional expressed directly in terms of the law $\mathcal{L}$ of a Gram-de Finetti array.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Lemma 6
nodes.statement: For each $M\geq 1,$ $\mathcal{L}\rightarrow \Psi_M(\mathcal{L})$ is a well-defined continuous function with respect to the weak convergence of the distribution $\mathcal{L}.$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
conclusions: $\mathcal{L}\rightarrow \Psi_M(\mathcal{L})$ is a well-defined continuous function with respect to the weak convergence of the distribution $\mathcal{L}.$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement: This is a generalization of Lemma 3 in \cite{Pan11:1} and can be verified exactly in the same way.
nodes.statement_short: Cite: the verification is identical to Lemma 3 of Panchenko (2011).
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Limit of $\Lambda_{M,N}(u^{M,N})$ in terms of $\Psi_M$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}^{M,N}$ and $\mathcal{L}^M$ be the distributions generating $R^{M,N}$ and $R^M$, respectively. Then Lemma $\ref{AGM:lem2}$ leads to \begin{align} \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\Lambda_{M,N}(u^{M,N})&=\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^{M,N})=\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Continuity of $\Psi_M$ identifies $\lim_N\Lambda_{M,N}(u^{M,N})$ with $\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Ultrametricity of the support of $G_M$
nodes.statement: Since the asymptotic Gibbs measure $G_M$ satisfies the G.G. identities $(\ref{AGM:eq4})$, the main result in $\cite{Pan11:4}$ implies that the support of $G_M$ is ultrametric with probability one, that is, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\left<I(R_{1,2}^M\geq \min(R_{1,3}^M,R_{2,3}^M))\right>_M=1. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Panchenko's ultrametricity theorem applies to $G_M$: overlaps satisfy the ultrametric inequality almost surely.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
assumptions: Since the asymptotic Gibbs measure $G_M$ satisfies the G.G. identities $(\ref{AGM:eq4})$
conclusions: the support of $G_M$ is ultrametric with probability one

nodes.name: Discretized overlap arrays $R_k^M$ and the measures $G_M^k$
nodes.statement: This implies that for any $q$, the inequality $q\leq \vtau^{\ell}\cdot\vtau^{\ell'}$ defines an equivalent relation and therefore, the array $(I(q\leq R_{\ell,\ell'}^M))_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}$ is nonnegative definite since it is block-diagonal with blocks consisting of all elements equal to one. Consider a sequence of functions $(H_k)_{k\geq 1}$ on $\left[0,1\right]$ by defining $H_{k}(q)=j/k$ if $j/(k+1)\leq q<(j+1)/(k+1)$ for $0\leq j\leq k$ and $H_k(1)=1.$ Then we see that $R_{k}^M=(H_k(R_{\ell,\ell'}^M))_{\ell,\ell\geq 1}$ is symmetric, weakly exchangable, and satisfies the G.G. identities. In addition, it is non-negative definite since it can be written as a convex combination of nonnegative definite arrays, \begin{align*} H_k(R_{\ell,\ell'}^M)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\frac{1}{k}I\left(\frac{j}{k+1}\leq R_{\ell,\ell'}^M\right). \end{align*} Thus by the Dovbysh-Sudakov representation, $R_{k}^M$ can be generated by a sample from a random measure $G_M^k$ on the unit ball of some Hilbert space. Since $\sup_{0\leq q\leq 1}|H_k(q)-q|\leq 1/k,$ $(R_k^M)_{k\geq 1}$ converges weakly to $R^M.$
nodes.statement_short: Discretizing overlaps by the step functions $H_k$ produces Gram-de Finetti arrays $R_k^M$, generated by measures $G_M^k$, that converge weakly to $R^M$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Convergence of $\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}_k^M)$
nodes.statement: From Lemma $\ref{AGM:lem2},$ we then obtain \begin{align} \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}_k^M)=\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M), \end{align} where $\mathcal{L}_k^M$ is the distribution for $R_k^M$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}_k^M)\to\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)$ as $k\to\infty$ by continuity of $\Psi_M$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Identification of $G_M^k$ with a Poisson-Dirichlet cascade
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from the Baffioni-Rosati theorem \cite{BR00}, an ultrametric measure, such as $G_M^k$, that satisfies the G.G. identities and under which the overlaps $R_k^M$ take finitely many values $(p/k)_{0\leq p\leq k}$ can be identified as the Poisson-Dirichlet cascade with parameters \begin{align*} \mathbf{m}^{M,k}&=(m_p^{M,k})_{0\leq p\leq k}\,\,\mbox{with $m_p^{M,k}=\mathbb{E}\left<I((R_k^M)_{1,2}\leq p/k)\right>_M,$}\\ \mathbf{q}^{M,k}&=(q_p^{M,k})_{0\leq p\leq k+1}\,\,\mbox{with $q_p^{M,k}=p/(k+1)$}. \end{align*} For details of this result, one may consult the proof of Theorem 15.3.6 in \cite{Tal11}. Let $\vx_k^M$ be the distribution function corresponding to this triplet $(k,\mathbf{m}^{M,k},\mathbf{q}^{M,k}).$ Using the same argument as Theorem 14.2.1 in \cite{Tal11}, we obtain \begin{align} \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}_k^M)=\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^M). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: A discretized ultrametric measure satisfying the G.G. identities is a Poisson-Dirichlet cascade, so $\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}_k^M)$ equals the Parisi functional $\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^M)$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
assumptions: an ultrametric measure, such as $G_M^k$, that satisfies the G.G. identities and under which the overlaps $R_k^M$ take finitely many values $(p/k)_{0\leq p\leq k}$

nodes.name: Lemma 7
nodes.statement: For any two triplets $(k,\mathbf{m},\mathbf{q})$ and $(k',\mathbf{m}',\mathbf{q}')$ associated with the distribution functions $\vx$ and $\vx'$ respectively, we have \begin{align} \left|\mathcal{P}_M(\vx)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx')\right|\leq \frac{\xi'(1)}{2}\int_0^1\left|\vx(q)-\vx'(q)\right|dq. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The Parisi functionals $\mathcal{P}_M$ are Lipschitz in the $L_1$ distance between distribution functions, uniformly in $M$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models
assumptions: For any two triplets $(k,\mathbf{m},\mathbf{q})$ and $(k',\mathbf{m}',\mathbf{q}')$ associated with the distribution functions $\vx$ and $\vx'$ respectively

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement: It is well-known that the same Lipschitz property as $(\ref{AGM:prop2})$ for the Parisi functional in the Ising spin glass model was established by F. Guerra \cite{Guerra03}. In the spherical models, despite of the non-product structure on the configuration space, one may find the same approach as Theorem 14.11.2 in \cite{Tal11} can also be applied to obtain $(\ref{AGM:prop2}).$
nodes.statement_short: Cite: Guerra's Ising argument, in the form of Theorem 14.11.2 of Talagrand (2011), transfers to the spherical model.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: The metric $d$ on $\mathcal{F}$ and the continuous extension of $\mathcal{P}_M$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the collection of all distribution functions $\vx$ on $\left[0,1\right]$. Define a metric $d$ on $\mathcal{F}$ by letting $d(\vx,\vx')=\int_0^1\left|\vx(q)-\vx'(q)\right|dq$ for every $\vx,\vx'\in \mathcal{F}.$ Using the Lipschitz inequality $(\ref{AGM:prop2})$, we can extend the functional $\mathcal{P}_M$ continuously to $\mathcal{F}.$
nodes.statement_short: Equip all distribution functions with the $L_1$ metric $d$; the Lipschitz bound extends $\mathcal{P}_M$ continuously to that space.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: If we denote by $\vx^M$ the distribution of $R_{1,2}^M,$ it follows that by using $(\ref{AGMU:add1})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq6})$, \begin{align} \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)=\mathcal{P}_M(\vx^M). \end{align} From Helly's selection theorem, $(\vx^M)_{M\geq 1}$ contains a weakly convergent subsequence with limit $\vx^\infty.$ For clarity, we simply use $(\vx^M)$ to denote this subsequence. Using $(\ref{AGM:prop2})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq7})$, if we set $\vx_k^\infty=H_k(\vx^\infty),$ then \begin{align*} \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^{\infty})\right| &=\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\mathcal{P}_M(\vx^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^{\infty})\right|\\ &\leq \frac{\xi'(1)}{2}\left(\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}d(\vx^M,\vx^{\infty})+d(\vx^\infty,\vx_k^{\infty})\right)\\ &=\frac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vx^\infty,\vx_k^{\infty}) \end{align*} for every $k\geq 1.$ To sum up, from $(\ref{AGM:eq2.1}),$ $(\ref{AGM:eq8})$, and this inequality, we conclude that \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N&\geq \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left( \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)+\frac{1}{M}\log\nu_M(A_\delta)\right)-\delta\xi'(1)\\ &\geq \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^\infty)-\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^\infty)\right|-\delta\xi'(1)\\ &\geq\inf_{\vx}\mathcal{P}(\vx)-\frac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vx^\infty,\vx_k^{\infty})-\delta\xi'(1) \end{align*} for every $k\geq 1$ and $\delta>0$ and this completes our proof by letting $\delta\rightarrow 0$ and $k\rightarrow\infty.$
nodes.statement_short: Extract a weak limit $\vx^\infty$ by Helly's theorem, control $|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^\infty)|$ by the Lipschitz bound, then let $\delta\to0$, $k\to\infty$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Identify $\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)$ with $\mathcal{P}_M(\vx^M)$
nodes.statement: If we denote by $\vx^M$ the distribution of $R_{1,2}^M,$ it follows that by using $(\ref{AGMU:add1})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq6})$, \begin{align} \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)=\mathcal{P}_M(\vx^M). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Let $k\to\infty$ in the discretized identity to get $\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)=\mathcal{P}_M(\vx^M)$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Extract a convergent subsequence by Helly's theorem
nodes.statement: From Helly's selection theorem, $(\vx^M)_{M\geq 1}$ contains a weakly convergent subsequence with limit $\vx^\infty.$ For clarity, we simply use $(\vx^M)$ to denote this subsequence.
nodes.statement_short: Helly's selection theorem gives a weak limit $\vx^\infty$ of the distribution functions $\vx^M$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models

nodes.name: Lipschitz control of $|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^\infty)|$
nodes.statement: Using $(\ref{AGM:prop2})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq7})$, if we set $\vx_k^\infty=H_k(\vx^\infty),$ then \begin{align*} \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^{\infty})\right| &=\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\mathcal{P}_M(\vx^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^{\infty})\right|\\ &\leq \frac{\xi'(1)}{2}\left(\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}d(\vx^M,\vx^{\infty})+d(\vx^\infty,\vx_k^{\infty})\right)\\ &=\frac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vx^\infty,\vx_k^{\infty}) \end{align*} for every $k\geq 1.$
nodes.statement_short: The Lipschitz bound reduces the discrepancy to $\tfrac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vx^\infty,\vx_k^\infty)$.

nodes.name: Conclude the lower bound
nodes.statement: To sum up, from $(\ref{AGM:eq2.1}),$ $(\ref{AGM:eq8})$, and this inequality, we conclude that \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N&\geq \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left( \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)+\frac{1}{M}\log\nu_M(A_\delta)\right)-\delta\xi'(1)\\ &\geq \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^\infty)-\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vx_k^\infty)\right|-\delta\xi'(1)\\ &\geq\inf_{\vx}\mathcal{P}(\vx)-\frac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vx^\infty,\vx_k^{\infty})-\delta\xi'(1) \end{align*} for every $k\geq 1$ and $\delta>0$ and this completes our proof by letting $\delta\rightarrow 0$ and $k\rightarrow\infty.$
nodes.statement_short: Chain the A.S.S. bound with the Lipschitz estimate and let $\delta\to0$, $k\to\infty$.
